# vitest-native

> Run your React Native tests under Vitest, against real React Native — the same JavaScript that ships in your app, mocking only the native-module boundary. That's the zero-config default. A fast pure-JS mock engine is available as an opt-in for RN-free unit tests. One plugin gives you both. Maintained successor to vitest-community/vitest-react-native, rebuilt for Vitest 5.

## Core idea

Two engines behind one plugin (`reactNative()`), so you choose the fidelity each suite needs:

- `engine: 'native'` (what the default `auto` resolves to in any RN or Expo app): runs real React Native JS, mocking only the thin native boundary: native modules and native host components. Jest's React Native preset mocks more than that (it also swaps View, Text, ScrollView, Image and Modal for stand-ins; both replace TextInput), so the real component JavaScript runs here. Needs `@react-native/babel-preset` (or, without it, Expo's preset) + `@babel/core` (present in any RN or Expo app). Highest fidelity.
- `engine: 'mock'`: a fast, zero-dependency pure-JS reimplementation of React Native. No Babel. For pure-logic suites, environment control, maximum determinism. Covers 100% of RN's stable public API.
- `engine: 'auto'` (the default): native when babel deps present, else mock.

A CI-gated behavioral cross-check runs the same assertions against both the mock and real RN across RN 0.86–0.88, keeping the mock honest.

## Evidence rules

Package capability and fidelity are defined only by package-owned conformance tests, behavioral crosschecks, packed consumer fixtures, version matrices, and the exact-version API compatibility check. Pinned external apps are observational tripwires only: they include custom migration configuration, dependency pins, snapshots, Jest-era mocks, fake timers, and other shims. Never infer that vitest-native regressed, a behavior is unsupported, or a migration is impossible from a bakeoff result alone. First reduce the behavior into a minimal package-owned test. See https://vitest-native.danfry.dev/guide/validation-model.

## Setup

Install: `npm install -D vitest vite vitest-native @testing-library/react-native` (vitest and vite are peers; RNTL is optional). `npx vitest-native init` writes the config; `npx vitest-native doctor` checks the setup.

vitest.config.ts:
```ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config'
import { reactNative } from 'vitest-native'
export default defineConfig({ plugins: [reactNative()] })
```

Requirements: Node 22.22.3+ (on 22), 24.12+ (on 24) or 26+, Vitest 5.x, Vite ^8.0.5, React 19, React Native 0.86–0.88 (native engine), Expo SDK 57 and 58. RNTL (@testing-library/react-native) 13–14 is an optional peer; auto-configured when installed. RNTL 14 makes render, fireEvent and act async: always `await render(...)` (a no-op on 13).

## Plugin options

`reactNative({ engine, platform, diagnostics, presets, mocks, assetExts, transform, hotRuntime, nativeModules, metroConfig })`
- engine: 'native' | 'mock' | 'auto' (default 'auto')
- platform: 'ios' | 'android' (default 'ios')
- presets: third-party library presets. Omit to auto-detect from installed deps; an array replaces auto-detection (`[]` disables all); an object such as `{ navigation: false }` switches presets off; a string inside either form is a path to your own preset module (`{ './my-preset.ts': true }` adds one)
- mocks: mock engine only (a non-empty value under native is a config error). JSON-serializable values only; each replaces that export whole. For components or functions use `vi.mock('react-native', ...)` in a setup file
- assetExts: extra asset extensions (loaded as Metro does: a registered asset id)
- transform: extra node_modules to transform (native engine; like Jest's transformIgnorePatterns)
- hotRuntime: 'auto' (default since 0.16: reuses workers across files where the run can be bounded) | false (a fresh worker per file, the default before 0.16) | true | options object. Experimental Vitest worker APIs; known differences from per-file isolation
- nativeModules: native engine only. 'device' (default; unregistered native modules are absent, as on a device) | 'permissive'
- metroConfig: experimental; use the project's Metro source-extension order and asset list

## Presets (auto-detected; most apply under both engines)

The full list, with the exact packages each preset shadows, is at https://vitest-native.danfry.dev/guide/presets#available-presets. Coming from Jest, delete a manual native-library mock only when a preset shadows that exact package. Under the native engine the `expo` preset is off unless enabled (`presets: { expo: true }` or listed in an array): Expo modules run their own JavaScript, as under jest-expo.

## Test helpers (`vitest-native/helpers`)

setDimensions, setColorScheme, setInsets, mockNativeModule, extendPresetMock, resetAllMocks (both engines). setPlatform is mock engine only (it throws under native; set `platform` in config). The mock engine's Keyboard/AppState also expose `_show`/`_hide`/`_setState`; native has no such methods.

## jest-compat (`vitest-native/jest-compat`)

For migrating existing Jest suites: jestCompatSetup (jest global backed by vi), jestMockTransform() (hoists top-level jest.mock), jestCompatAliases() (@jest/globals shim + jest-native no-op). Clears mechanical Jest-API coupling; per-suite cleanup (snapshots, suite-specific mocks) still required.
